label: Dependence and independence of assertion errors in preface arguments
term: dependence and independence of assertion errors
resolution: Preface arguments use 'independent' and 'dependent' in at least three senses. ERROR_DEPENDENCE_1 (shared-only): every assertion expresses one shared condition, so errors are entirely common-mode and the assertions are logically dependent. ERROR_DEPENDENCE_2 (isolated): the shared condition is certain and assertions fail only through mutually independent local error opportunities; only here does P(all true) = q^n hold. ERROR_DEPENDENCE_3 (truth-independent check): absence of a check's flag is probabilistically independent of what it checks, so the check supplies no discriminating evidence. Senses 1 and 2 are contrasted, not bridged: the comparison results show that a joint probability computed under sense 2 cannot be carried over to a bundle in sense 1, which is why their argument is a sense-mixing control. Sense 3 concerns a check's relation to its target, not the relation among assertions. None of these senses is the logical independence of propositions, and none is attributed to the Truth Core corpus.
